NORMALIZED (wording-only): The claim misdescribes the subject. The high_not case (tests/connectors/test_row_rule_additions_mysql.py:137,143) passes init_command="SET SESSION sql_mode = 'HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE'" into _chain, which forwards it to MySQLRunner (tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:190-202) together with remove_sql_modes=RULE_SET_REMOVED_SQL_MODES. RULE_SET_REMOVED_SQL_MODES contains HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE (src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:67). In MySQLRunner (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:126-139), each query runs after init_command. The runner reads @@SESSION.sql_mode, drops the removed flags, and issues SET SESSION sql_mode before the query. So the rule SQL does NOT run under a session whose sql_mode includes HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE. The claim's first assertion is false. The claim's conditional ('if the factory strips...') describes what actually happens, and the test does hold, since it checks that the stripping works. No source requires the claimed property. Criterion 3 (criteria.json) says the connection 'starts with' HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, and the test does start the connection that way. The strip logic is correct on every input a shipped caller can produce, and no repository rule requires the rule SQL to run under that mode.

rule_sets.py:636-643 builds Not(Paren(Is(col, NULL))) with the comment in question. MySQL 8.0 docs (Operator Precedence / HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE): by default NOT ranks below comparison operators including IS, so NOT x IS NULL is NOT (x IS NULL). With HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NOT binds tighter than comparison operators, so NOT x IS NULL is (NOT x) IS NULL. The docs' example is NOT a BETWEEN b AND c becoming (NOT a) BETWEEN b AND c, and IS is at the same comparison level. The comment matches this. I did not run MySQL, so this rests on the documented precedence only. The code also parenthesizes, so it is correct under both modes.
